name: In-situ combustion and solvent-assisted SAGD
principle: Air injection burns part of the oil in the reservoir to generate heat; THAI (toe-to-heel air injection) pairs a vertical air injector with a horizontal producer. Solvent-assisted variants (VAPEX, eMSAGP, LASER) add vaporised solvent or liquid to steam. Romania's Suplacu de Barcau field has run in-situ combustion since 1970 to 1971 with over 55% recovery.

reference_plants.capacity: THAI (toe-to-heel air injection) pilot; per-well production and injection data published by the operator; numeric capacity not stated on the public data page

source.note: Petrobank Kerrobert THAI public data page (Saskatchewan, Canada; production history, KP2/KA2 well data). 50/50 Petrobank-Baytex JV reported Jan 2010; read 2026-10-28

notes: Process provenance: Documents the ISC sequence - oxygen-containing gas (air or oxygen-enriched air) injected through an injection well, ignition by autoignition, downhole gas burner, electric heater or pyrophoric agent, then a forward combustion front moving with airflow through burned zone, combustion front, cracking/vaporization, steam plateau, water bank and oil bank to the producer; wet combustion adds water. Solvent-assisted SAGD is not covered on this page.
